facts.title: SAT-Edge-Agent: Hardware-in-the-Loop Edge-Agent Orchestration for Onboard Satellite Intelligence
facts.event_hint: arXiv:2608.03728v1 reports a reproducible hardware-in-the-loop satellite edge-agent orchestration boundary
facts.problem: Onboard satellite intelligence must translate mission intent into local tool calls, expose execution state, and return structured mission artifacts under communication, power, and intermittent-contact constraints. A detector alone does not provide this routing, artifact, and operator-facing response layer.
facts.mechanism: SAT-Edge-Agent runs a browser workspace and FastAPI agent backend on a COTS ARM-based heterogeneous edge SoC. The backend decides when image-grounded evidence requires a local YOLO-style oriented-object detector, exposes its structured FAIR1M-metadata-backed artifact as the authoritative machine-facing tool event, optionally asks a local OpenAI-compatible language service for a narrative, and streams start/tool/token/done state over SSE. This separates machine consumption from replaceable language synthesis while preserving per-request success, invalid-input, and partial-batch error fields.

evidence.claim: Two fixed FAIR1M workloads (single image and serial two-image) each completed all 20 measured attempts; mean Full-Agent latency was 29.353 s and 60.937 s, with empirical nearest-rank P95 of 31.166 s and 66.882 s.
evidence.condition: n=20 attempts per workload; warm-ups excluded; serial pair invoked images serially.

evidence.claim: Detector execution averaged 861.386 ms for the single image and 1510.920 ms cumulatively for the serial pair, representing 2.93% and 2.48% of the corresponding Full-Agent means.
evidence.condition: YOLO-tool duration measured inside the end-to-end Full-Agent request window.

evidence.claim: Mean time to the first visible response token was 16.184 s for the single image and 28.785 s for the serial pair; this interval includes agent and tool activity and is not pure LLM first-token latency.
evidence.condition: Profiler-enabled successful runs; detector time is nested inside the interval.

evidence.claim: Mean sampled CPU utilization was 20.761% and 20.482%; a 200-ms devfreq/sysfs NPU-load field read 100% for both workloads, but the field is shared by the detector and local language service and is not detector-only occupancy.
evidence.condition: Resource fields sampled over each Full-Agent request; NPU value is a coarse shared-accelerator software field.
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.11, Table 6; PDF p.12, HIL and Measurement Boundary

evidence.claim: The HIL host is a COTS ARM-based heterogeneous edge-SoC board with aarch64 Debian 11, eight Cortex-A55 cores, and 31 GiB memory; the workflow returns structured OBB detections and metadata-backed geographic fields before optional narrative synthesis.
evidence.condition: Sanitized runtime snapshot and representative FAIR1M service contract; exact board, private weights, and model identities are withheld.
evidence.source_locator: PDF pp.5-8, HIL Boundary/Table 3 and Service-Contract Evidence

facts.evaluation_context: This is a ground-based hardware-in-the-loop evaluation on a sanitized COTS ARM edge-SoC runtime. The repeated protocol uses one fixed FAIR1M image and one fixed serial two-image workload, 20 measured attempts each, with warm-ups excluded. Full-Agent latency covers routing, detector invocation, result handling, annotated-output production, local response formation, and SSE delivery; detector time is measured separately. The paper reports success completion, latency, CPU/NPU telemetry, structured output, invalid-file handling, and a 1/2 partial-batch case.
facts.limitations: The study is not an in-orbit, radiation-qualified, or flight-computer demonstration. It reports no detector mAP or new geolocation accuracy, because geographic fields are propagated from FAIR1M-style metadata. Measurements cover only one fixed single image and one fixed serial pair with n=20, so they do not establish broad workload generalization, robust P99 tails, concurrency behavior, or larger-batch performance. The first-token interval is not isolated to language-model latency; frontend and internal substages remain unisolated. Power evidence is an unsynchronized plug-meter pilot, not calibrated energy per request. Timeout, retry, watchdog, restart, and comprehensive fault-recovery behavior are not established, and private board/model/weights limit hardware-normalized comparison.
facts.project_relevance: For agent infrastructure, the strongest signal is that detector time is only about 2–3% of end-to-end latency in these workloads, so routing, request construction, tool-result handling, response formation, and streaming are the larger optimization boundary. The machine-facing structured tool event can be consumed without waiting for narrative generation, but the paper does not provide a controlled schema-only versus narrative-enabled latency ablation; treating deferred synthesis as a measured speedup would be an unsupported inference.
source_notes: Primary arXiv PDF was fetched and the title matches the input metadata exactly.
The paper explicitly bounds its claims to fixed-workload HIL orchestration rather than detector accuracy, calibrated energy, or flight readiness.
